scenarios.name: Redis Service Failure (substitute)
scenarios.audienceSees: Chat shows Reconnecting and messages stop crossing between windows; video keeps playing.
scenarios.realWorldCause: Memory exhaustion, host restart or a bad Redis upgrade.
scenarios.failure: SIGKILL Redis. Chat fan-out, presence and viewer counts lose their shared bus.
scenarios.recovery: The Healer starts Redis; both APIs reconnect. PostgreSQL chat history stays intact.
scenarios.prerequisites: Use an isolated demo with a healthy database and both APIs. Redis persistence is disabled: volatile keys and Pub/Sub deliveries can be lost; PostgreSQL history stays intact.

scenarios.name: Video Gateway Crash
scenarios.audienceSees: Every viewer's video freezes and the stall timer counts up, then resumes by itself.
scenarios.realWorldCause: Connection exhaustion or a bad configuration reload.
scenarios.failure: SIGKILL the single HLS entry point. Every viewer's playlist and segment requests fail.
scenarios.recovery: The Healer starts the gateway and verifies advancing segments fetched through it.
scenarios.prerequisites: Healthy edges and origins. A live stream makes the freeze visible.

scenarios.name: Crash the whole API tier (website down, video survives)
scenarios.audienceSees: The site shows Can't reach the server, retrying; chat disconnects; live video keeps playing.
scenarios.realWorldCause: A bad deployment, a memory leak or an unhandled crash.
scenarios.failure: SIGKILL API-1 and API-2 in one experiment. No application server is left.
scenarios.recovery: The Healer starts API-1, then API-2 (one operation at a time); both are verified serving.
scenarios.prerequisites: Both APIs, PostgreSQL and Redis healthy; Healer budget available for both APIs.

scenarios.name: Crash ingest relay (broadcaster drops)
scenarios.audienceSees: Studio shows Reconnecting, viewers see Broadcaster reconnecting, then the stream is LIVE again.
scenarios.realWorldCause: A malformed incoming stream or ingest overload.
scenarios.failure: SIGKILL the MediaMTX ingest relay. Browser WHIP and OBS RTMP publishers are disconnected.
scenarios.recovery: The Healer starts the relay. The broadcaster client reconnects itself; that is recorded separately.
scenarios.prerequisites: Healthy origins. A live broadcaster makes the drop and the return visible.

scenarios.name: Freeze API-2 (hung, not crashed)
scenarios.audienceSees: Pages and chat sends become slow (up to the 10 s gateway timeout), then return to normal.
scenarios.realWorldCause: A deadlock, an infinite loop or a stuck query.
scenarios.failure: SIGTSTP the API-2 Node process: the container stays running but stops answering.
scenarios.recovery: The Observer sees timeouts, the Healer corroborates the hang and restarts API-2 (not start).
scenarios.prerequisites: API-1 must be healthy so restarting API-2 never removes the last serving instance.

scenarios.name: Traffic Surge / Overload
scenarios.audienceSees: Load meter and latency climb, pages slow down, then Served by API-3 appears and latency drops while load continues.
scenarios.realWorldCause: A flash crowd, bots or a retry storm.
scenarios.failure: A bounded load generator floods the API tier with simulated viewers for a bounded time.
scenarios.recovery: The Healer adds the pre-provisioned spare API-3 (scale-out) and removes it again after load stays normal.
scenarios.prerequisites: Healthy tier, the spare API-3 created but stopped, and Healer budget for API-3.

scenarios.name: API Server Crash
scenarios.audienceSees: Nothing breaks; the Served by badge shows API-2 only, then API-1 again.
scenarios.realWorldCause: An unhandled crash on one instance.
scenarios.failure: Terminate API-1 with SIGKILL. Its current requests may disconnect.
scenarios.recovery: API-2 serves surviving requests; the independent Healer starts and verifies API-1.
scenarios.prerequisites: Both APIs, PostgreSQL, Redis and fresh monitoring must be healthy.

scenarios.name: Edge Node Failure
scenarios.audienceSees: Video keeps playing; the overlay flips Served by Edge-1 to Edge-2, later Edge-1 again.
scenarios.realWorldCause: Cache node crash or disk/memory pressure on one edge.
scenarios.failure: Terminate the selected HLS edge. Viewers may briefly buffer.
scenarios.recovery: Existing routing uses Edge-2; the Healer verifies restored HLS segments.
scenarios.prerequisites: A genuine live source, healthy peer/origins and progressing media.

scenarios.name: Kill primary origin
scenarios.audienceSees: The overlay shows Source: Primary to Standby, possibly with a short reinit.
scenarios.realWorldCause: Origin process crash or a failed media host.
scenarios.failure: Terminate primary MediaMTX. The player may reinitialize on standby.
scenarios.recovery: Standby preserves the source; the Healer restores primary without forced failback.
scenarios.prerequisites: Live publishing and independently verified healthy standby media.

scenarios.name: Network Latency / Connection Disruption
scenarios.audienceSees: Recommendations slow down, then the circuit protects callers until latency ends.
scenarios.realWorldCause: A congested or degraded network path to a partner API.
scenarios.failure: Add real downstream latency to the private recommendation connection.
scenarios.recovery: The owned fault expires; bounded safe-read probes verify real reconnection.
scenarios.prerequisites: Healthy simulated dependency, closed circuit and functioning expiry adapter.

scenarios.name: Interrupt external API demo
scenarios.audienceSees: Recommendations show an explicit unavailable fallback instead of hanging.
scenarios.failure: Reset connections to the explicitly simulated read-only recommendation API.
scenarios.recovery: Real circuit opens and rejects calls, then probes after timed fault cleanup.
scenarios.prerequisites: Closed circuit and healthy simulated upstream. No payments or writes.

scenarios.name: Database outage
scenarios.audienceSees: Sign-in and writes would fail until an operator acts.
scenarios.realWorldCause: Disk failure, corruption or a bad migration.
scenarios.failure: Would interrupt database-dependent authorization and writes.
scenarios.recovery: Current policy escalates storage faults for operator review.
scenarios.prerequisites: A separate disposable database fault/cleanup authority is required.
scenarios.reason: Disabled: no database fault or automatic database restoration authority is granted.

scenarios.name: Interrupt test broadcaster
scenarios.audienceSees: The stream would go offline until the broadcaster returns.
scenarios.realWorldCause: Camera unplugged, laptop asleep or home internet loss.
scenarios.failure: Would stop a publisher owned by the test environment.
scenarios.recovery: Only an authorized broadcaster can return the original source.
scenarios.prerequisites: A controller-owned disposable publisher lifecycle is required.
scenarios.reason: Disabled: the controller does not own your OBS, camera or FFmpeg process.
